rate_per_tonne.description: Most common structure for contract crushing. Contractor is paid a fixed or escalating rand-per-tonne rate for crushed and screened material delivered to spec. Incentivises throughput efficiency.
rate_per_tonne.typical_application: Quarry, aggregate, and run-of-mine coal crushing

day_rate.description: Equipment and crew hired on a daily or hourly rate regardless of throughput. Preferred by clients for variable or uncertain feed. Contractor bears less volume risk.
day_rate.typical_application: Short-term campaigns, peak demand supplementation, pilot operations

LSTK.description: Lump-Sum Turn-Key: Contractor designs, supplies, installs, commissions, and (sometimes) operates a complete crushing and screening plant for a fixed price. High risk for contractor but premium margin if well scoped.
LSTK.typical_application: New mine or quarry greenfield plant installations

EPCM.description: Engineering, Procurement & Construction Management: Contractor manages the project on behalf of the owner but costs are reimbursable. The mining house owns all equipment. Reduces contractor balance sheet risk vs. LSTK.
EPCM.typical_application: Major mine expansion crushing plant upgrades; used by DRA Global, Worley, Hatch

hybrid_rpt_plus_mobilisation.description: Rate-per-tonne with a separate mobilisation and demobilisation allowance. Ensures contractor recovers plant setup costs even on lower-volume campaigns.
hybrid_rpt_plus_mobilisation.typical_application: Remote mine sites, seasonal quarry operations
